analysis.title: U S Capital Markets Perspectives (September 30, 2026)
key_insights: The US enters Q4 2026 with above-trend growth, above-target inflation and a Fed that has resumed hiking. The Fed raised rates 0.25% on September 16, 2026, and FOMC members and markets anticipate further hikes.

Inflation has overtaken the labor market as the Fed's immediate concern. September CPI rose 0.6% m/m and 3.7% y/y, driven by energy and gasoline. Shelter, wage and service costs keep inflation sticky.

The 10-year Treasury yield is up 132 basis points since the start of the Iran War and reached 5.29% on 9/30/2026. Term premium and real yields are rising alongside nominal yields, which the report attributes to resilient growth, heavy AI capex and large government debt supply.
Hyperscalers have issued over $180B of debt in 2026 to fund AI infrastructure. Fed Chair Warsh and Treasury Secretary Bessent have said this borrowing competes with the $31 trillion Treasury market.

AI investment is a major growth driver. AI-related investment added 1.34 percentage points to Q1 2026 GDP growth, and the report says the AI boom is still climbing after year three, which is later than prior investment booms peaked.

Global GDP is projected at 3.0% for 2026 per the IMF, with US GDP at 2.2% annualized in Q2. Oil went above $100 per barrel after the Iran War began and has traded on both sides of $100. The ECB, BOJ and Fed have begun raising rates, while the BoE held.

The September labor report is described as a goldilocks print from the Fed's standpoint. Jobs growth slowed but remains positive, unemployment rose to 4.2%, and initial claims fell to 197,000, near a 57-year low. The report calls this a low-hire, low-fire market.

ISM Manufacturing PMI was 54.5 and ISM Services was 54.9 in September. The ISM services price index is back near mid-2022 levels, and tariffs, metals, energy and supply constraints keep goods inflation elevated, limiting room for rate cuts.
August consumer spending rose 0.8% m/m (real +0.6%, the largest gain since March 2025) while personal income rose only 0.2%. The saving rate fell to 4.1%. One-year inflation expectations are rising.
Stock-bond correlation is rising with inflation. Bonds helped in only two of the five S&P 500 pullbacks since 2024. In the three inflation-scare selloffs (tariffs, oil, Iran) bonds fell with stocks.

Equity leadership: the Mag 7 rebounded in 2H 2026 after lagging in 1H. YTD through 9/30 the S&P 500 High Beta, Momentum and Pure Growth factors lead, and defensive factors (Low Volatility, High Dividend) lag. The S&P 500 is up 12.7% YTD.
The US dollar is up 3.2% YTD through 9/30/2026 and gold is down 3.6%. Gold is pressured by dollar strength, but the report cites central bank diversification and ETF inflows as structural support.

Midterm seasonality: the S&P 500 has had positive Q4 returns in 20 of 23 midterm years, with a median of 7.90%. The three negative Q4s (1978, 1994, 2018) all coincided with Fed Funds increases, which is relevant now that the Fed is hiking. Midterm elections are November 3.

Federated Hermes forecasts (as of October 15, 2026): 2026E real GDP 2.3%, core CPI 2.8%, 10-year yield 5.00%, Fed funds upper limit 4.25%, S&P 500 EPS $370 and an S&P 500 target of 8,500. For 2027E: GDP 2.9%, 10-year 4.75%, Fed funds 4.50%, EPS $425 and a target of 10,000.

Four scenarios are laid out with associated asset classes. Resilient growth favors US all-cap equity, intermediate bonds and municipals. Inflation persistence favors dividend and value equity and floating-rate or sub-1-year bonds. Productivity-led growth favors growth equity, EM and high yield. A hard landing favors alternatives, money markets and government bonds.

Hard-landing risk indicators: the Leading Economic Indicators index fell to 99.5 in August, labor force participation is 61.8% versus 62.5% a year earlier, and the JOLTS hire rate is subdued at 3.3%. The report names a persistent Iran War and energy shock as a possible catalyst, with inflation limiting the Fed's response.
Key dates: September jobs report Oct 2, September CPI Oct 14, FOMC decision Oct 28, Q3 GDP advance Oct 29, midterms Nov 3, FOMC with projections Dec 9.
earnings_insights: Federated Hermes forecasts S&P 500 EPS of $370 for 2026E and $425 for 2027E, versus $274 in 2025A. These are the firm's own estimates, not reported figures.
The report says strong earnings, led by AI-related business investment, are a key driver of the S&P 500, and projects strong earnings growth through 2027.

risk_factors: Persistent inflation from energy, freight, food, tariffs and shelter, with further Fed hikes anticipated.
A prolonged Iran War and energy shock could trigger a US hard landing while inflation limits the Fed's response.
Rising Treasury yields and term premium, with heavy hyperscaler debt issuance competing with Treasuries.
Stocks and bonds can fall together when inflation drives selloffs, which weakens bonds as a hedge.
Potential fiscal policy changes after the November 3 midterm elections.
Cooling labor indicators: participation rate down to 61.8%, subdued JOLTS hire rate and a declining Leading Economic Indicators index.
Elevated consumer inflation expectations and a falling saving rate as spending outpaces income.
charts_described: Chart of AI-related investment: the text states AI-related investment contributed 1.34 percentage points to the economy's 2% growth in Q1 2026.
Chart of the Treasury yield curve: the text states the 10-year yield reached 5.29% on 9/30/2026, up 132 basis points since the start of the Iran War.

vol_and_positioning: Midterm election years have historically shown elevated volatility. The S&P 500's average intra-year drawdown in midterm years is cited as deeper than in other years of the cycle.
The S&P 500 has not declined in the 12 months following a midterm election since 1942.
YTD through 9/30/2026, High Beta (+29.6%) and Momentum (+27.8%) are the top S&P 500 factors, and Low Volatility is the weakest (+0.6%).
In September, Momentum (+3.2%) and High Beta (+3.1%) rebounded strongly after weakness earlier in the quarter.
geopolitical: The Iran War has produced energy supply shocks. Oil rose above $100 per barrel after the war began, and the 10-year Treasury yield is up 132 basis points since it started.
Energy shocks from the Iran War are prompting central banks (ECB, BOJ, Fed) to raise rates, while the Bank of England has held.
The report names a prolonged Iran War and energy shock as a possible catalyst for a US hard landing.
US midterm elections on November 3, 2026 are cited as a source of potential fiscal policy change.
Tariffs are cited as a driver of elevated goods inflation.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient growth with AI capex support, near-full employment (4.2% unemployment), claims near a 57-year low and 2.2% Q2 GDP growth. The Fed's September projections put 2027 GDP at 2.4%.
tension_points.bear_case: Sticky inflation limits the Fed's response to a downturn. The Leading Economic Indicators index fell to 99.5, participation is down to 61.8%, the JOLTS hire rate is subdued and yields at 5.29% are tightening conditions. An energy shock from the Iran War could freeze the labor market.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A persistent Iran War and energy shock that deteriorates the labor market, which the report names as a possible hard-landing catalyst.
